questions.scenario: Your younger sibling is trying to secretly open your phone. What do you do?

options.text: I intentionally leave it unlocked but set a fake app trap to catch them red-handed.
I check my 'Screen Time' and background apps to see exactly what they tried to open.
I set up a complex App-Lock, hide the photos folder, and change the wallpaper to a warning.
I loudly threaten them that I will tell Mummy if they ever touch my phone again.

questions.scenario: You are playing a multiplayer game and someone is using speed-cheats. Your reaction?

options.text: I try to figure out how they installed the cheat and try to hack them back.
I record their gameplay, collect their ID details, and report them with proof.
I build a safe defensive base in the game where their cheats cannot reach me.
I rally my team, make a strategy to avoid them, and focus on surviving.

questions.scenario: A friend's Instagram account gets hacked and starts sending spam links.

options.text: I try sending fake links back to the hacker to see if I can trace their IP.
I analyze the spam message to figure out exactly how the phishing link works.
I immediately go to my own settings and turn on Two-Factor Authentication (2FA).
I warn all our mutual friends in the WhatsApp group to not click the link.

questions.scenario: When you watch a spy or heist movie (like Mission Impossible or Dhoom), what excites you?

options.text: The scene where the hero bypasses lasers, cracks the safe, and breaks in.
The detective finding a single, tiny clue that solves the whole mystery.
The complex vault design and the high-tech security system protecting the money.
The mastermind boss who plans the entire operation from a secret room.

questions.scenario: You have a secret diary where you write your personal thoughts. How do you protect it?

options.text: I write it in a secret code language that only I can read.
I place a small hair or thread on the book to check if someone opened it.
I buy a diary with a strong combination lock and a solid metal cover.
I hide it in a place where nobody would ever think to look, like under the mattress.

questions.scenario: The school Wi-Fi is blocked for students. What is your move?

options.text: I try using a VPN, change proxy settings, or find a loophole to connect.
I check the network settings to see which specific websites the school has blocked.
I don't mind. I like that the school network is perfectly structured and safe from viruses.
I convince the computer teacher to give me the password for an 'important project'.

questions.scenario: You get an SMS saying 'You won 1 Crore Lottery! Click here'.

options.text: I open the link on an old, empty phone just to see what kind of scam they built.
I check the sender's number and search it on Truecaller to find the fraudster's location.
I block the number and tweak my phone's spam filter settings to block all such SMS.
I tell my parents about it so they don't fall for the same scam.

questions.scenario: You lose your house keys. How does your brain work to find them?

options.text: I try to pick the lock with a hairpin or find an open window to break into my own house.
I trace my exact steps backward, analyzing every place I visited since morning.
I decide to make 3 spare keys tomorrow and distribute them to family members safely.
I call a locksmith, negotiate the price, and get the job done.

questions.scenario: Papa buys a new Wi-Fi router for the house. What do you do?

options.text: I try to log into the admin panel using 'admin/admin' to see if I can control it.
I check the speed test logs to see if we are getting the exact speed Papa paid for.
I set up a strong custom password, hide the Wi-Fi name, and create a separate 'Guest' network.
I make a strict rule about who gets the password and who doesn't in the house.

questions.scenario: What kind of puzzle games do you like on your phone?

options.text: Escape Room games where I have to break out of a locked prison.
Detective games where I have to find hidden objects and clues.
Games where I have to connect pipes, circuits, or build a safe fortress.
Strategy games where I have to manage resources and lead an army.

Ethical_Hacker.title: Ethical Hacker / Penetration Tester
Ethical_Hacker.primary_match_text: You have a brilliant, rebellious mind! You love finding loopholes, breaking rules (legally), and thinking exactly like a hacker to beat them.
Ethical_Hacker.day_in_the_life: Trying to hack into your own company's systems to find weaknesses before the bad guys do.
Ethical_Hacker.alternative_match_text: Because of your quick thinking and ability to bypass systems, you would also make an excellent Game Tester or Tech Troubleshooter.
Ethical_Hacker.roadmap: Take Science (PCM) in 11th/12th. Pursue a B.Tech in Computer Science or specialized Cyber Security certifications like CEH.

Security_Analyst.title: Cyber Security Analyst / Digital Forensics
Security_Analyst.primary_match_text: You are a digital detective. You have a sharp eye for detail, you love investigating clues, and you never let a mistake go unnoticed.
Security_Analyst.day_in_the_life: Monitoring networks, investigating how a cyber-attack happened, and recovering stolen data like a digital police officer.
Security_Analyst.alternative_match_text: Your strong investigative skills make you a perfect fit for Intelligence Agencies (IB/RAW) or Data Analytics.
Security_Analyst.roadmap: Take Science (PCM) in 11th/12th. Pursue a B.Tech in CSE, B.Sc in Forensic Science, or Cyber Forensics.

Security_Architect.title: Security Architect / Network Defender
Security_Architect.primary_match_text: You are the ultimate protector. You love building strong defenses, setting up safe environments, and ensuring no one can break in.
Security_Architect.day_in_the_life: Designing unbreakable security systems, setting up firewalls, and writing code that protects banks and top-secret apps.
Security_Architect.alternative_match_text: If you ever step away from security, your structural mindset is perfect for becoming a Cloud Architect or Core Software Developer.
Security_Architect.roadmap: Take Science (PCM) in 11th/12th. Pursue a B.Tech in IT or Computer Science.

Security_Manager.title: Information Security Officer (CISO)
Security_Manager.primary_match_text: You are a natural leader who understands both tech and people. You know how to make rules, manage crises, and lead a team to safety.
Security_Manager.day_in_the_life: Making security rules for the whole company, training employees not to click on fake links, and managing the cyber defense budget.
Security_Manager.alternative_match_text: With your commanding nature and tech knowledge, you would easily excel as an IT Project Manager or Tech Startup CEO.
Security_Manager.roadmap: Take Commerce or PCM in 11th/12th. Pursue a B.Tech or BCA, followed by an MBA in IT Management.
